answer: Each agent may propose trades freely, but only agents with a history of settled exchanges can endorse a new identity. An endorsement is backed by a small bond that is slashed if the newcomer defaults, so one operator cannot cheaply mint a crowd of trusted accounts: they must build distinct settlement histories and risk capital across them. The velvet ledger keeps those bonds visible at the ledge of each market, while a falcon audit samples linked accounts for circular trades that fake reputation.
